{{nihongo|'''Tamanooya Shrine'''|玉祖神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Tamanooya Shrine''' (たまのおやじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kozaki|Q11590720|qid=Q11590720|lt=Kozaki}}, {{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is also called "Tamanooya Myojin" and "Takayasu Daimyojin."

It is the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of the eastern Yao {{ill|Takayasu|Q11669131|qid=Q11669131|lt=Takayasu district}} (13 former villages of old Takayasu District excluding the Onji area).

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Akama-no-Mikoto}} (also called Kushi-Akama-no-Mikoto)

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it began in 710 (Wado 3) when a divided spirit was invited from {{ill|Tamanooya Shrine (Q11572731)|Q11572731|qid=Q11572731}} in {{ill|Suō Province|Q1053037|qid=Q1053037}}. At that time the deity is said to have landed at {{ill|Suminoe no Tsu|Q3503628|qid=Q3503628}}, stayed at {{ill|Onji Shrine|ja|恩智神社|qid=Q11492258}}, and then been enshrined at the present site. Because people of the Tamatsukuri-be lived in this area, it is thought that their ancestral deity was enshrined here. The current shrine buildings are said to have been rebuilt in 1725 (Kyoho 10).

=== Festivals ===
Every year in mid-July (weekend nearest the 15th and 16th), each district brings out futon-daiko drums for the festival. In 2010 (Heisei 22), the shrine marked its 1300th year and held a grand commemorative festival.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Property (national) ===
* Wooden prohibition placard with inscription "Bunji 1, 12th month" (old document)
*: Said to be the prohibition placard displayed at Onkoji, the shrine-temple of Tamanooya Shrine, and regarded as Japan's oldest surviving kinsai (prohibition order), issued by {{ill|Hōjō Tokimasa|arz|هوجو توكيماسا|ca|Hōjō Tokimasa|ckb|ھۆجۆ تۆکیمەسا|de|Hōjō Tokimasa|es|Hōjō Tokimasa|fa|هوجو توکیماسا|fr|Hōjō Tokimasa|hi|होजो टोकिमासा|id|Hōjō Tokimasa|it|Hōjō Tokimasa|ja|北条時政|ko|호조 도키마사|nl|Hojo Tokimasa|pl|Tokimasa Hōjō|pt|Hōjō Tokimasa|ru|Ходзё Токимаса|th|โฮโจ โทกิมาซะ|tr|Hōjō Tokimasa|uk|Ходзьо Токімаса|vi|Hōjō Tokimasa|zh|北條時政|qid=Q589811}} in December 1185 (Bunji 1)<ref name="八尾市文化財2">[http://bunka.city.yao.osaka.jp/detail/index?cultural_id=9 Tamanooya Shrine Wooden Prohibition Placard - Yao City Cultural Property Information System], accessed 2019-02-10</ref>. Deposited at Yao City Museum of History and Folklore. Designated April 20, 1910 (Meiji 43)<ref>Home Ministry Notification No. 68, April 20, Meiji 43</ref><ref>{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9546|Wooden prohibition placard with inscription "Bunji first year twelfth month"}}</ref>.

=== Osaka Prefecture designated cultural properties ===
* Tangible cultural properties
** Tamanooya Shrine wooden male and female deity statues (sculpture) - seated wooden statues once treated as shintai. Designated as Osaka Prefecture important art objects in 1965 (Showa 40){{refnest|group=注釈|This designation is under the Osaka Prefecture rule for preserving and honoring old cultural memorials, and differs from national "Important Art Objects" recognized under the {{ill|Law Regarding the Preservation of Important Works of Fine Arts|ja|重要美術品等ノ保存ニ関スル法律|qid=Q11644864}}.}}. Designated as Osaka Prefecture tangible cultural property on February 20, 1970 (Showa 45)<ref name="一覧">[https://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/bunkazaihogo/bunkazai/hunai-siteiichiran.html List of designated cultural properties in Osaka Prefecture] (Yao City file).</ref>.
* Natural monument
** Camphor tree of Tamanooya Shrine - designated February 20, 1970 (Showa 45)<ref name="一覧"/>.

=== Yao City designated cultural properties ===
* Tangible cultural property
** Tamanooya Shrine main hall (with ridge tags) (building) - designated March 1, 2016 (Heisei 28)<ref name="一覧"/>.

=== Other ===
The shrine preserves items such as a flute said to have been used by the Heian poet {{ill|Ariwara no Narihira|Q451991|qid=Q451991}} and a stone lantern donated by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyori|Q313641|qid=Q313641}}.
